channel.title: Resistance Daily
channel.description: A non-partisan daily record of human-rights and civil-liberties events in India and around the world. Every fact links to its source.

item.title: Resistance Daily · Tue 10 Nov 2026
item.description:
• Baramulla: Baramulla men acquitted after six years under UAPA. A J&K special UAPA court acquitted two men held since 2020 over an alleged grenade recovery, calling the evidence inconsistent. Police had said arms were found at a highway checkpoint.
  • Uttar Pradesh: UP told to trace bailed prisoners still jailed. In 20 UP districts, 106 of 264 undertrials granted bail remain jailed over surety conditions. The Supreme Court ordered the state to identify such prisoners in 55 more districts and secure their release.
  • Maharashtra: Maharashtra churches cancel or limit children's Bible camps. Some churches cancelled or limited Diwali Bible camps to Christian children after nine FIRs followed prayer-meeting disruptions and a new anti-conversion law. No police or government response was reported.
  • Bengaluru: Group flags high voter deletions in Karnataka seats. A Muslim community body said 27.59% of voters were deleted in 10 Karnataka seats held by Muslim MLAs during the revision, against 19.45% statewide. No Election Commission response was reported.
  • Turkey: Steel plant blast kills 17 workers in Turkey. An explosion at the Habaş iron and steel plant in Aliağa killed at least 17 workers and injured 12, officials said. The governor said a crane collapsed during furnace maintenance.
  • Crete: Thirteen migrants die as boat sinks off Crete. At least 13 people died when a migrant boat sank off Crete; the coastguard rescued 18, all Sudanese. Authorities said the boat had likely been at sea for days in strong winds.
  • Harare: Harare demolitions leave families who bought plots homeless. Council records list over 5,000 Harare houses facing demolition under 37 court orders; residents say they bought plots through council processes. The council says it is enforcing planning rules.
  • Moscow: Russia's Novaya Gazeta closes after eviction. Novaya Gazeta held its final editorial meeting on Monday and closed after being evicted from its offices. The Kremlin called the closure part of "a standard rotational process".
  • Macao: Macao ex-lawmaker Au Kam San jailed 12.5 years. A Macao court sentenced democracy activist Au Kam San under the national security law after a closed trial. The court says he worked with hostile overseas groups; HRW calls the charges baseless.
  • Gaza: Two still missing after Gaza tent landslide. Two people remain missing after Sunday's sandbank collapse that killed five in Deir el-Balah. Save the Children says Israel has blocked caravans promised under the ceasefire; no Israeli response was reported.
  • Sudan: Lawyer: army should not hold ICC suspect Haroun. Sudanese lawyer Muaz Hadra said police and courts, not the army, should hold Ahmed Haroun, who faces war-crimes charges at home and an ICC warrant. No army comment was reported.

item.title: Resistance Daily · Mon 9 Nov 2026
item.description:
• Delhi: No protest request accepted since Jantar Mantar closed. None of 15 protest applications filed at Parliament Street police station since 5 September was accepted, a police officer said. Groups say moving to the alternative grounds police named proved far from easy.
  • Dibrugarh: Oil India fire toll rises to four workers. A fourth contract worker died on Sunday after a 6 November blast and fire at an Oil India tank farm; three are critical. Oil India suspended four site staff pending a high-level inquiry.
  • Bengaluru: Bengaluru slum residents report blocked pensions, papers. Legal aid camps near Jayanagar found widows' pensions cancelled and certificates refused; some residents alleged police demand ₹3,000–4,000 to settle minor disputes. No police response was reported.
  • Mansa: Slain anti-drug activist cremated after family protest. Parvinder Singh Jhota, shot dead on 13 October while on Facebook Live, was cremated after his family ended a 22-day protest. The state gave the case to the CBI and suspended three officials.
  • Sudan: Sudan's army detains ICC suspect Ahmed Haroun. Sudan's military detained Ahmed Haroun, wanted by the ICC over alleged Darfur crimes, his lawyers and party said; reports differ on where. No army statement was reported; it refused past ICC handovers.
  • Gaza: Sandbank collapse in Gaza storm kills five. Heavy rain collapsed a sandbank onto tents in Deir el-Balah, killing five including four children, local health authorities said. Save the Children blamed Israeli limits on shelter supplies; no Israeli response was reported.
  • Senegal: Migrant boat sinks off Senegal, killing 34. A pirogue carrying migrants capsized off northwestern Senegal on Saturday, killing at least 34, the state press agency said. The interior ministry said one person was rescued and searches continue.
  • Amsterdam: Over 200,000 march in Amsterdam over Gaza. More than 200,000 people marched in Amsterdam's 'Red Line' protest seeking curbs on trade and arms sales to Israel, organisers including Amnesty Netherlands said. No police count was reported.
  • Israel: Palestinian journalist freed after five days uncharged. Israel released journalist Abed Abou Shhadeh after five days' detention without charge on suspicion of "contact with a foreign agent". His lawyers at Adalah said police had no evidence; no official comment was reported.
  • Ukraine: Russian strikes cut power to 850,000 Ukrainians. Overnight Russian strikes on energy sites left over 600,000 people in Dnipropetrovsk region and 250,000 in Kharkiv region without power, Ukrainian officials and the provider DTEK said. No Russian comment was reported.

item.title: Resistance Daily · Sun 8 Nov 2026
item.description:
• Siang: Four Siang dam protesters freed after 29 days. Four Geku villagers held under Arunachal's anti-terror law since 9 October were freed as a state "goodwill gesture" before talks. Six others remain detained; the state says FIR withdrawals must follow legal process.
  • Golaghat: Kaziranga activist Pranab Doley walks free. Land-rights activist Pranab Doley left Golaghat jail on Friday evening after the High Court quashed his NSA detention. He called the NSA's use arbitrary; no Assam government response was reported.
  • Old Delhi: Six workers die in Old Delhi building collapse. Six workers from Bihar died when an unauthorised building under construction collapsed in Chawri Bazar. Police arrested the owner on Saturday and three contractors on Friday on culpable homicide charges.
  • Sribhumi: Assam says police expelled 28 alleged Bangladeshis. Assam's chief minister said Sribhumi police detected and expelled 28 people they describe as Bangladeshis living illegally. The report names no court or tribunal process; no Bangladeshi response was reported.
  • Sanaa: Strikes on village near Sanaa kill 27. Strikes on al-Shariya village north of Sanaa killed at least 27 people, mostly women and children, Houthi health officials said, blaming the Saudi-led coalition. Saudi Arabia and Yemen's government have not commented.
  • Gaza: First winter storm floods Gaza's tent camps. The season's first storm flooded about 70,000 tents of displaced families, Gaza's media office said; aid groups blame Israeli limits on shelter materials. No Israeli response was reported.
  • France: Cost-of-living protests sweep France again. About 146,000 people protested across France, the interior ministry said; unions said 250,000. Police fired tear gas in Paris and Lyon and say 200 people attacked officers during an arrest.
  • Blue Nile: Fear grows in Damazin as fighting spreads. Damazin residents reported power, water and grain-mill cuts and families fleeing as fighting spread in Blue Nile; one resident said the city was calm. No army or RSF statement was reported.
  • El Hierro: Canary island declares emergency over boat arrivals. El Hierro declared an emergency and asked Madrid for help after more than 3,300 people arrived on about 30 boats since 1 November. No central government reply was reported.

item.title: Resistance Daily · Sat 7 Nov 2026
item.description:
• Kaziranga: Court quashes NSA detention of Kaziranga activist. The Gauhati High Court quashed land-rights activist Pranab Doley's NSA detention, saying it rested on "stale" cases. Assam had cited foreign visits and funds; no government reply to the ruling was reported.
  • Srinagar: Mirwaiz kept home, barred from Friday sermon. Mirwaiz Umar Farooq said he was under house detention for a sixth day and barred from leading Friday prayers, after a sermon on political prisoners. No police or official statement was reported.
  • Delhi HC: X says 'imposter' sent account takedown notices. X told the Delhi High Court an imposter, not Delhi Police, sent notices to remove IFF and SFLC accounts; the accounts stay and the case was closed. Police did not comment on record.
  • Kangpokpi: Kangpokpi shutdown over killing of two Kuki men. A Kuki-Zo body's shutdown over the killing of two Kuki civilians closed Kangpokpi for a fourth day and was extended 48 hours. Police say extra forces are deployed; no state reply was reported.
  • Patna: Police kill three wanted men near Patna. A Bihar STF and Patna Police team shot dead three men wanted over an October shooting, in Sherpur village. Police say they fired in self-defence after being shot at.
  • Belagavi: Belagavi cane farmers suspend, not end, protest. Sugarcane farmers suspended their agitation after factories offered ₹3,600 a tonne and profit-sharing, but still seek ₹5,500 and a state incentive. No state government reply was reported.
  • Taiz: Strikes on Yemen market kill dozens. Strikes on a Taiz market killed at least 30 civilians, Houthi health officials said, blaming Saudi air strikes; government forces blamed Houthi missiles. The Saudi-led coalition did not respond.
  • North Kivu: Village raid kills 33 in Ebola-hit Congo. Attackers killed 33 people and burned a health post in Cantine, local civil society said; 180 patients, including Ebola cases, fled. Local authorities blame the ADF armed group.
  • Sudan: UN: Sudan's shelter aid warehouses are empty. UNHCR and IOM said 15.4 million Sudanese need emergency shelter but funds cover about 10%; 936,000 have been helped. "Our warehouses are completely empty," IOM's Sudan chief said.
  • Tanzania: Tanzania jails opposition leader Lissu for incitement. A court cleared Tundu Lissu of treason but jailed him four years for incitement over his slogan "No Reforms, No Election". He calls it political; Amnesty called it a "travesty of justice".
  • Macau: Macau jails ex-lawmaker in first security case. Ex-lawmaker Au Kam San, 69, got 12½ years for subversion after a closed-door trial. Prosecutors said he worked with "external hostile organisations"; his wife called it "groundless persecution".
  • Hebron: Hebron's Ibrahimi Mosque closed to Palestinian worshippers. Israeli forces barred Palestinian worshippers and staff from the mosque from Friday afternoon to Saturday night for a Jewish observance. Forces said they expected about 20,000 visitors and deployed hundreds of personnel.

item.title: Resistance Daily · Fri 6 Nov 2026
item.description:
• Siang: Siang dam opponents refuse talks until detainees freed. A farmers' forum rejected the chief minister's offer of talks on 5–7 November until detainees are freed and armed forces withdrawn; a foot march heads to Itanagar. No government reply was reported.
  • Raj Ghat: Police remove Ankita Bhandari's parents from Raj Ghat. Police detained the parents of Ankita Bhandari, killed in 2022, at Raj Ghat late Wednesday; her father says they were dragged. Police cite a prohibitory order against a planned indefinite sit-in.
  • Delhi HC: Rights groups challenge police bid to remove accounts. Two digital rights groups asked the Delhi High Court to quash reports purportedly from Delhi Police asking X to remove their accounts; police have neither confirmed nor withdrawn them, the groups say.
  • Farrukhabad: Court orders FIR against officer over arrest papers. The Allahabad High Court found an investigating officer later added arrest grounds to Mohd Yaseen's papers, freed him and ordered an FIR against the officer. The state said the grounds were supplied and signed.
  • Supreme Court: 24-hour clock starts at detention, court rules. The Supreme Court ruled the 24-hour limit to bring someone before a magistrate runs from detention, not formal arrest, and freed four Tripura drug-case accused held about 21 hours first. No state reply was reported.
  • Delhi riots case: Umar Khalid, Sharjeel Imam seek Supreme Court bail. Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam appealed against the Delhi High Court's 30 September bail denial; Imam says none of 47 protected witnesses has been examined. Police allege a larger conspiracy behind the 2020 violence.
  • Khartoum: Security summons two striking teachers in Khartoum. Security services summoned two teachers in Ombada over alleged incitement of a strike now in its third week, the Sudanese Teachers Committee said; no statement from the authorities was reported.
  • Sanctions: Australia sanctions Sudan's army and RSF leaders. Australia imposed sanctions and travel bans on army chief al-Burhan, RSF leader Dagalo and two others, citing attacks on civilians, torture and killings; no response from those named was reported.
  • Gaza: Israeli fire kills four in Gaza, including child. Israeli drone strikes and fire killed at least four Palestinians, including a child in Bureij camp, medical sources said on Thursday; no Israeli military comment was reported.
  • Biddu: Five homes demolished in Biddu. Israeli forces demolished five homes in Biddu, displacing more than 100 Palestinians, Al Jazeera reported on Thursday; residents said they had tried to stop it in court. No Israeli reason was reported.
  • France: Hundreds of thousands march in France; 448 detained. Between 575,000 (Interior Ministry) and 1.6 million (CGT) marched for higher wages; police used tear gas in Lyon and Paris and detained 448. The government defended police and said any abuses would be investigated.
  • California: California commutes all 548 death sentences. Governor Newsom commuted all 548 California death sentences to life without parole, saying state killing is "incompatible with California's values"; about two-thirds need state Supreme Court review first.

item.title: Resistance Daily · Thu 5 Nov 2026
item.description:
• Noney: Gunfight between Naga armed groups kills 3–4. Three to four suspected members of rival Naga armed groups were killed in a gunfight in Noney district early Wednesday, officials and residents say; reports differ on the toll and several were injured.
  • Delhi: Supreme Court frees man held weeks after bail. The Supreme Court ordered Uttar Pradesh to free a man still jailed weeks after it granted him bail on 28 September, and to show why he should not be compensated; no state explanation was reported.
  • Kalady: Kerala court bars suspended protesting students from exams. Kerala's High Court barred 16 students suspended after an August campus protest from exams, citing attendance rules and saying dharnas have "no place" on campuses; the students have moved the Supreme Court.
  • Yellapur: Thousands block highway against Karnataka river-link plan. More than 10,000 people blocked the Hubballi–Karwar highway in Yellapur on Tuesday against the Bedthi–Aghanashini river-linking plan, ETV Bharat reported; no state or central government response was reported.
  • Bengaluru: Karnataka court quashes case over rally slogan. Karnataka's High Court quashed a case against a man who shouted a pro-Pakistan slogan at a 2022 Mandya rally, accepting it was a slip of the tongue; prosecutors had alleged intent to cause unrest.
  • Kordofan: Drone strikes kill at least 14 civilians. Drone strikes killed at least 14 civilians in West and South Kordofan and Blue Nile on Monday and Tuesday, residents told Radio Dabanga; a Blue Nile group blames the RSF, which had no reported response.
  • Hong Kong: Joshua Wong jailed for 10 more years. A Hong Kong court sentenced democracy activist Joshua Wong, 30, to 10 years for conspiring to collude with foreign forces; authorities say the security law keeps stability, while HRW calls the charges baseless.
  • Rafah: Gunfire hits tents at Rafah displacement site. Gunfire hit tents at a displacement site in northern Rafah on Tuesday, reportedly injuring people and forcing an aid group to leave, OCHA said; no Israeli military comment was reported.
  • Yatenga: Armed group killed 27 civilians, HRW finds. The Al-Qaeda-linked group JNIM killed at least 27 civilians in two September attacks in Yatenga province, HRW said on Wednesday; JNIM told HRW the victims were members of government-allied militias.
  • Narayanganj: Police tear-gas striking garment workers. Police fired tear gas and stun grenades at garment workers demanding higher pay on Wednesday, with dozens injured in Fatullah, media report; officials say a new wage board's pay scale starts in January.

item.title: Resistance Daily · Wed 4 Nov 2026
item.description:
• Delhi: Police say Jantar Mantar unfit as protest site. Delhi Police told the Supreme Court on Tuesday that Jantar Mantar, a public road holding about 1,500 people, should never have been a protest site; petitioners say de-notifying it violates free assembly.
  • Bengaluru: High Court takes up killings of Karnataka lawyers. Karnataka's High Court opened a PIL on Tuesday over violence against lawyers, including two October murders, asking the state how it handles lawyers' complaints against police; no state response was reported.
  • Sivasagar: Guwahati shooting accused killed in police custody. Ghanakanta Gogoi, accused in the 26 October Guwahati hotel shooting that killed five, died when police fired during his transfer in Sivasagar; police say he tried to seize an officer's pistol. No inquiry was reported.
  • Pulwama: Court: encrypted app no ground for PSA detention. The J&K High Court quashed the Public Safety Act detention of a Pulwama man held since July 2025 over alleged militant contacts, saying use of an encrypted app was no adequate basis for detention.
  • Madhubani: Bihar police officer fires on villagers, one dead. A police ASI fired his service pistol at villagers in Madhubani district early Tuesday, killing one and injuring three, police say; he has been suspended, faces a murder case and is absconding.
  • Ahmedabad: 61 alleged undocumented migrants detained in Ahmedabad. Police detained 61 people, including women and children, in Ahmedabad on Monday as alleged undocumented immigrants, mostly Bangladeshi, they say; officials say deportation proceedings are under way.
  • North Darfur: Drone kills two travellers in North Darfur. A drone struck a vehicle in Wadi Majrur, Al-Malha locality, on Sunday, killing two civilians, a local rights monitor told Radio Tamazuj; it blames the army, and no army response was reported.
  • Zaporizhzhia: Bombs hit Ukrainian aid centre, 33 dead. At least 33 people died when aerial bombs hit an aid distribution centre in Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia, on Monday, Ukrainian officials say; Russia's defence ministry says it targeted military units.
  • Gaza: Girl killed in drone strike on Gaza tent. Three Palestinians, including a girl hit when a drone struck a tent in Gaza City, were killed on Tuesday, medical sources told Anadolu; no Israeli military comment was reported.
  • Rakhine: World Court to rule in Myanmar genocide case. The International Court of Justice will rule on 19 November in Gambia's case accusing Myanmar of genocide against the Rohingya, over 700,000 of whom fled in 2017, HRW said; no Myanmar comment was reported.
  • Addis Ababa: Ethiopia suspends one of its oldest newspapers. Ethiopia's Media Authority indefinitely suspended the Reporter, the last private Amharic newspaper, on 2 November, accusing it of content against "national interests"; HRW calls it part of a wider media crackdown.
  • Bangkok: Two Uyghurs face deportation from Thailand, HRW warns. Two Uyghur men held in Thailand since 2014 were moved to Bangkok immigration detention ahead of possible return to China, HRW said on Tuesday; Thai officials told MPs China had demanded their return.

item.title: Resistance Daily · Tue 3 Nov 2026
item.description:
• Upper Siang: Internet cut in Upper Siang during dam shutdown. A 36-hour shutdown against the proposed Siang dam began on Monday demanding detainees' release, and internet was suspended in four Upper Siang areas "to curb misinformation", Arunachal Times reports; Chief Minister Pema Khandu said "we are not talking about dam construction at this stage".
  • Torsa: Bulldozers clear Torsa tea garden protest site. Bulldozers cleared a 100-day protest site of about 80 families at Torsa Tea Garden in north Bengal on Monday for the proposed Jaigaon land port, and 11 people were detained, The Statesman reports; the families seek rehabilitation, the case is before the Calcutta High Court, and no official response was reported.
  • Mumbai: Court says OCI cardholders cannot protest. The Bombay High Court said on Monday that Overseas Citizen of India cardholders have no right to protest and asked actor Imran Khan, a US citizen detained at a 10 October Mumbai protest, to apologise, Scroll reports; he apologised, and the court kept on hold a notice ordering him to leave India.
  • Anantapur: Police shoot Andhra suspect, say he fled. Police in Anantapur district shot a man arrested on Sunday over a chainsaw attack on a schoolgirl, saying they fired in self-defence when he threw stones and tried to flee; he is in serious condition, Scroll reports, and no inquiry has been reported.
  • Kassala: Drone strikes cut power across eastern Sudan. Drones hit three substations in Kassala and near Merowe on Monday, cutting power, and at least 16 power stations were targeted in a week, Anadolu reports; Sudan's government accuses Ethiopia of involvement, Ethiopia gave no immediate comment, and the RSF generally does not comment.
  • Sudan: Sudan law puts journalists at risk, CPJ says. CPJ said on Monday that a 19 October change to Article 51 of Sudan's Criminal Act, criminalising online or media support for threats to state security, could bring journalists life in prison or death; the journalists' syndicate warned of prosecutions, and the army did not answer CPJ.
  • Gaza: Israeli fire kills five in Gaza, medics say. Israeli strikes and fire killed five Palestinians on Monday in Gaza City, al-Mawasi, Khan Younis and east of Deir al-Balah, medical sources told Anadolu; Gaza's government media office counts 1,593 killed since the October 2025 ceasefire, and no Israeli military comment was reported.
  • Mrauk-U: Air strikes hit Myanmar clinic and school. Military air strikes on Sunday killed at least 12 people in Rakhine State, including a week-old baby at a maternity clinic in Mrauk-U, and three students at a Loikaw school, an armed group, an aid worker and monitors told Reuters; the military government did not immediately respond.
  • Dhaka: Garment workers clash with police over wages. Thousands of garment workers seeking a 30,000-taka minimum wage clashed with police around Dhaka on Monday, with tear gas used and at least 57 arrested and 58 police injured, AFP reports; the government formed a wage board, and the home minister warned of an "iron hand".
  • Isfahan: Iran sets execution of two young protesters. Iran scheduled the execution of Amirhossein Maleki, 20, and Abolfazl Ebrahimi, 18, in Isfahan on 3 November over January's protests, rights groups told ABC News; authorities accuse them of involvement in killing four security personnel, while a defence lawyer says none was charged with murder.

item.title: Resistance Daily · Mon 2 Nov 2026
item.description:
• Dhubri: Dhubri eviction drive displaces over 4,000 people. Authorities in Assam's Dhubri district demolished the homes of more than 640 Bengali Muslim families on Sunday, displacing over 4,000 people, officials told Scroll. The district commissioner said the land is meant for an industrial park and claimed most residents have land elsewhere; one resident says he has lived there since 1962.
  • Senapati: Two missing Kuki men found dead in Manipur. Manipur Police said on Sunday that two Kuki civilians missing from Taphou Kuki village since Wednesday were found dead, Scroll reports, taking deaths in Naga-Kuki clashes since February to 68. Naga groups led by the NPO question the recovery's timeline and seek an impartial inquiry; no police response to them was reported.
  • Ujjain: Four workers die in Ujjain hotel waste chamber. Four men died of suspected suffocation late on Saturday inside a food-waste chamber at a hotel on the Ujjain-Dewas Road, and two who tried to rescue them fell ill. Police are investigating, officials are checking whether safety precautions were in place, and the state announced ₹4 lakh for each family.
  • Karjat: Karjat forest families left out of project clearance. About 150 mostly Katkari families who live off Saidongar forest were never recorded as forest-dependent, so a 3,000 MW Torrent Power project was cleared with no rehabilitation planned, The Indian Express found. About 1,100 trees were felled before a pause; a forest officer says the gram sabha never submitted records.
  • Blue Nile: Blue Nile's displaced short of food, medicine. Displaced people in Sudan's Blue Nile state told Radio Tamazuj on Sunday that aid falls short as food and medicines run low and disease spreads. The state aid commissioner puts the displaced at about 27,400 (Dabanga reports the figure as families) and says WFP and others are delivering food, cash and hygiene kits.
  • Gaza: Israeli strikes kill eight in Gaza, hospitals say. Hospitals said Israeli strikes on Sunday killed three people, including a four-year-old boy, near a school in Gaza City, and five police officers in al-Mawasi, Khan Younis. The Israeli military said it struck military operatives but gave no details; Gaza's health ministry counts 1,580 killed since the ceasefire.
  • Hebron: Hebron operation has displaced almost 5,000. Al Jazeera reported on Sunday that almost 5,000 people have been displaced since Israel's military operation in Hebron began on 23 October, after two Israeli soldiers were shot. UNICEF counts over 480 families displaced, including more than 1,800 children. Israel's defence minister says residents cannot return until operations end.
  • Kambove: Congo police detain over 500 at Kambove mine. Police in Haut-Katanga said more than 500 people were detained in a special operation at the Kambove mining site near Likasi, Actualité.cd reported on Sunday. The provincial police chief said it targeted people illegally occupying public-service roles at the site; no charges or access to lawyers were reported.
  • Ukraine: Russian strikes cut power as Kherson truce ends. President Zelensky said Russian strikes on energy sites in four regions overnight into Sunday left hundreds of thousands of homes without power; a strike killed two, including a girl of 13, in Vinnytsia region. A six-day local truce around Oleshky in Kherson ended Sunday night. No Russian comment on the strikes was reported.
  • Perth: WA police face-scanning trial checked 1.38 million faces. Western Australia Police said a five-month live facial-recognition trial that ended on Saturday scanned 1,380,882 faces, leading to 122 arrests and nine false alerts. The commissioner said no one wrongly flagged was arrested; Civil Liberties Australia criticised how police presented the error rate.

item.title: Resistance Daily · Sun 1 Nov 2026
item.description:
• Delhi: Siang dam protesters detained in Delhi. Delhi Police detained protesters, including activist Katon Moyong, outside Arunachal Bhawan on Saturday as they opposed the Siang dam. Organisers say about 40 were held and allege some were sexually assaulted; some were later released. No Delhi Police response to the allegations was reported.
  • Manipur: Three Kuki men killed in Noney gunfight. Three Kuki men were killed on Saturday in a gunfight between armed groups at Kekru Naga village, police said, adding that security had been stepped up. The Kuki Inpi Manipur said the dead were village volunteers and blamed Naga armed groups; police have not identified those responsible.
  • Mangolpuri: Four workers die in Delhi shoe factory fire. Four workers died in a fire at a shoe factory in Mangolpuri; relatives allege they were made to work extra hours in the festive season. Police arrested two management members on Saturday and filed an FIR for culpable homicide and negligence against the owner and others.
  • Bengaluru: Playwright smeared with ink during Gandhi play. Protesters objecting to a play's portrayal of Mahatma Gandhi smeared ink on playwright Addanda Cariappa during a show in Bengaluru on Saturday. A complaint has been filed at Banashankari police station and police say investigations are on; the protesters' own complaint seeks action against Cariappa.
  • Press: Journalist's website taken offline by host. Hosting firm Hostinger suspended journalist Paranjoy Guha Thakurta's website on 28 October over a "Fraud/Scam" abuse report, days after a court ordered one 2019 article removed in a defamation suit. In a statement on Saturday he called it backdoor censorship; Hostinger support said suspension was "not negotiable".
  • Delhi: Tribunal says July protest policing was excessive. A people's tribunal of retired civil servants, chaired by former judge Anjana Prakash, reported on Saturday that Delhi Police used disproportionate force and arbitrary mass detentions against July's exam-leak protests. It heard 25 people; Delhi Police and the Rapid Action Force were invited but did not respond.
  • Sudan: UN chief condemns escalating Sudan drone strikes. On Saturday UN Secretary-General Guterres, through his spokesman, condemned escalating drone attacks by the parties in Sudan, after Monday's strike on Nyala's Tanqonj market killed at least 102 people. The strike has been attributed to the army. No army or RSF response was reported.
  • Gaza: Four Palestinians die in Gaza despite ceasefire. Hospitals said Israeli shelling of Nuseirat killed a teacher, a man died of earlier strike wounds, and two girls died after a tent fire of unclear cause in al-Mawasi. Gaza's health ministry counts 1,580 killed since the ceasefire. No Israeli military comment was reported.
  • France: Police fire tear gas at French youth protests. Authorities counted 320,000 marchers on Saturday's cost-of-living and schools protests, organisers nearly half a million. Police used tear gas in Paris and Lyon and the interior ministry reported at least 290 arrests. The government says it has heard protesters and is studying cost-of-living measures.
  • London: London police arrest 139 at Palestine Action protest. Police arrested 139 people at a protest outside the US embassy against the ban on Palestine Action, mostly for expressing support for a proscribed group, the Metropolitan Police said. Organisers Defend Our Juries call the vigils peaceful and say arrests under the ban now exceed 4,000.
  • Yemen: UN rights chief seeks probe into detainee death. UN rights chief Volker Türk demanded an independent investigation into the death of staffer Mohammad el Shami, held by Houthi authorities since June 2024, whose family learned of it weeks late. The UN says 71 personnel remain detained. No Houthi response was reported.
  • Germany: Gen Z protests spread across German cities. Youth-led rallies on Saturday over living costs, education cuts and conscription drew 5,000 in Berlin by police count and 10,000 by organisers, who claim 100,000–120,000 nationwide. Police used water cannon in Cologne, saying their measures targeted violent individuals, not peaceful participants.

item.title: Resistance Daily · Sat 31 Oct 2026
item.description:
• Delhi: Supreme Court upholds bail for Khurram Parvez. The Supreme Court on Friday dismissed the NIA's challenge to bail for Kashmiri activist Khurram Parvez in a UAPA terror-funding case, citing his long incarceration since his November 2021 arrest. The High Court had granted bail in July after nearly four and a half years; the NIA's arguments were not reported.
  • Bengaluru: Vigilante group confronts migrant workers; 19 held. Members of the group Rashtra Rakshana Pade entered a shed housing labourers in Hulimangala, near Bengaluru, on 28 October, accusing them of being illegal Bangladeshi migrants, and a fight followed. Police arrested 19 people from both sides on complaints and counter-complaints; a police release says the workers maintain they are from West Bengal.
  • Guwahati: Guwahati protest backs Siang dam opponents. Citizens protested outside Nehru Park in Guwahati on Friday against the Upper Siang dam in Arunachal Pradesh, demanding the release of arrested Adi leaders and protesters. Arunachal police report 69 arrests after the 23 October violence; no official response to the Guwahati protest was reported.
  • Sudan: Investigators name 25 commanders over wartime rape. The Centre for Information Resilience, a UK open-source group, says it has reasonable grounds to believe 25 commanders of the RSF, the army and allied forces were directly or indirectly responsible for sexual violence at five sites, including El Fasher and Gezira. Neither force responded to Al Jazeera; both have denied such abuses.
  • Gaza: UN: Gazans pushed into ever smaller areas. The UN rights office said on Friday Israeli military zones in Gaza are expanding west, pushing Palestinians into smaller areas; a 25 October drone strike and fire at tents in Al Shujaiyeh displaced about 800 people. Israel has said it aims to deploy across 70 per cent of Gaza; no Israeli comment was reported.
  • West Bank: Olive pickers attacked; two harvesters arrested. Settlers beat a Palestinian man in Burqa and attacked olive pickers and a foreign activist in Kafr Malik on Friday, where soldiers arrested two Palestinian harvesters, according to reports citing Wafa; troops fired sound grenades at pickers in Al-Lubban Al-Sharqiya. No Israeli military comment was reported.
  • Moscow: Novaya Gazeta says it is forced to close. Novaya Gazeta, Russia's best-known independent newspaper, said on Friday it will close on 9 November because authorities and security services forced it to; it reports being evicted from its Moscow office. UN rights chief Volker Türk called it a devastating blow to independent media. No Kremlin comment was reported.
  • Kathmandu: Police detain journalists without warrants. Plainclothes police in Kathmandu took at least two journalists, Bishwamani Subedi of Nepal Press and editor Shovaraj Baral, for questioning on Friday without showing warrants or stating grounds. The Prime Minister's office said it had no prior knowledge and ordered their release; the Press Council demanded the legal basis.
  • DR Congo: 28.8 million face acute hunger in Congo. About 28.8 million people in DR Congo, 23 per cent of those analysed, face high acute food insecurity through December, a new IPC alert says, with North Kivu, South Kivu and Ituri hardest hit. It cites conflict, displacement, an Ebola outbreak and falling aid. No government response was reported.

item.title: Resistance Daily · Fri 30 Oct 2026
item.description:
• Siang: Siang dam opponents march; 200+ get notices. Opponents of the Siang dam marched on Thursday, demanding its cancellation and the release of those in custody. Police say 69 people are arrested in 53 cases and over 200 served notices; the state says current work is only feasibility surveys.
  • Jamia: Jamia agrees to student polls after protest. Jamia Millia Islamia agreed on Thursday to hold students' union elections, not held since 2006, and revoked action against protesters, ending an 18-day protest. Students say police detained over 70 of them and that they were pressured to sign; an FIR was filed on the university's vandalism complaint.
  • Delhi mosque: Delhi mosque demolition on hold for four weeks. The Union government told the Delhi High Court on Thursday it will take no coercive action for four weeks against the Race Course mosque near the Prime Minister's residence while it decides a Waqf Board representation. Its notice calls the mosque unauthorised, on government land; the NDMC lists it as heritage.
  • Bombay HC: Court: activist's 2011 re-arrest violated rights. The Bombay High Court ruled that activist Arun Ferreira's 2011 re-arrest at Nagpur jail's gate, as he left after acquittals, violated his rights to liberty and to be told the grounds, and ordered Maharashtra to pay ₹2 lakh. The state had argued due process was followed.
  • Sudan: UNICEF: five children killed in Nyala strike. UNICEF said on Thursday at least five children were killed in Monday's drone strike on a Nyala market. A Yale lab reports a near-total absence of civilian life in El Fasher a year after the RSF took it. No army comment was reported; the RSF says life there is normal.
  • Gaza: Six killed in Gaza, including ministry staff. Gaza's Health Ministry said six people were killed in 24 hours. A drone strike on a car near Maghazi camp killed two on Thursday, and the toll from Wednesday's strike on an Economy Ministry post in al-Mawasi rose to four employees. No Israeli military comment was reported.
  • Dnipro: Drone strike on Dnipro rail station kills 13. A jet-powered drone hit a platform at Dnipro's main railway station on Thursday as a train for Zaporizhzhia was boarding, killing 13 people, officials said; the UN says 10 were injured and condemned the attack. No Russian comment was reported.
  • Myanmar: UN expert: military killed 8,384 civilians since coup. A UN special rapporteur said on Thursday that Myanmar's military has killed at least 8,384 civilians since the 2021 coup, about 753 of them during its '100-day peace plan' this year, and called attacks on civilian infrastructure deliberate. No military response was reported.
  • West Bank: Activists attacked by settlers are arrested, banned. Israeli police arrested two activist-journalists after footage showed settlers, one armed, attacking them near Umm al-Kheir overnight Wednesday; they were released but banned from the West Bank for the rest of the year. Police cite an alleged attempt to steal weapons; no settlers were reported arrested.

item.title: Resistance Daily · Thu 29 Oct 2026
item.description:
• Pasighat: 69 arrested under Arunachal anti-terror law. Police say 69 people have been arrested and four detained under Arunachal's Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act over the 23 October arson in Pasighat, in 55 cases. A minister met representatives of 72 villages on the dam and said local communities' rights must stay central.
  • Karnataka: Karnataka voter roll shrinks by nearly one crore. Karnataka's final voter roll, published on 27 October after a special revision, lists about 4.55 crore electors, nearly one crore fewer than before; Bengaluru's fell from about 1.03 crore to 59.08 lakh. The Chief Electoral Officer says deletion forms covered electors found ineligible at hearings, and denies bulk filings without reasons.
  • Muzaffarnagar: Dalit man killed; wife's brother arrested. Akshay, a 23-year-old Dalit man who married against his wife's family's wishes, was beaten with bricks in Khatauli on Monday and died on Tuesday. Police arrested two people on Wednesday, including her brother, and say the killing appears premeditated.
  • Supreme Court: Foreign nationality alone no bar to UAPA bail. The Supreme Court ruled on 27 October that the UAPA's bail bar for foreigners applies only if the prosecution shows the accused entered India illegally, dismissing the Union government's appeal against bail for a Sri Lankan national.
  • Sudan: UN warns Kordofan sieges risk new atrocities. A year after the RSF seized El Fasher, UN officials warned on Wednesday that sieges in Kordofan and Blue Nile could bring new atrocities; UN investigators said they found hallmarks of genocide in El Fasher. No army or RSF response was reported; the RSF says El Fasher is safe for civilians.
  • Gaza: Five killed in Gaza strikes after Israeli vote. Israeli strikes in Rafah and Khan Younis killed five people on Wednesday, Gaza's civil defence agency and a hospital said, three of them in a drone strike in Rafah. The Israeli army said it 'struck terrorists in the area'.
  • Hebron: Hebron operation now affects about 5,000 people. About 780 families, roughly 5,000 people, have been displaced or are trapped at home as Israel's Hebron operation entered its sixth day, the city's municipality says. The army began it after two soldiers were killed on Friday; no Israeli comment on the figures was reported.
  • Cairo: Egypt court orders Mada Masr shut. A Cairo court ordered the independent outlet Mada Masr closed and fined editor Lina Attalah 3 million Egyptian pounds for running an unlicensed website. She was held for hours until the fine was paid and faces a retrial on 11 November over a 2024 sentence. No official comment was reported.
  • Jakarta: Tear gas at Jakarta protest over graft, fires. Thousands protested in Jakarta and four other cities on Wednesday over corruption and the handling of wildfires, seeking a national emergency. Police fired tear gas in Jakarta after bottles were thrown. The government said it understands the students' concerns.

item.title: Resistance Daily · Wed 28 Oct 2026
item.description:
• Pasighat: Curbs stay in Pasighat; detained activist's health worsens. About 30 companies of central armed police are deployed across three Siang districts, and Pasighat's district magistrate says curbs on gatherings stay 'until further orders'. Activist Ebo Mili's family says his health is worsening in custody, where he is reportedly on hunger strike; he denies any role in the arson.
  • Mumbai: Court pauses actor's 'Leave India' notice. The Bombay High Court on Tuesday kept in abeyance until 2 November a notice telling actor Imran Khan, an OCI cardholder, to leave India by 28 October after he joined a protest. The Additional Solicitor General sought more time and orally assured the court Khan would not have to leave meanwhile.
  • Bengaluru: Groups set deadline on Bengaluru protest curbs. Civil society groups and unions gave Karnataka until 26 November to withdraw the 2021 order that confines most Bengaluru protests to Freedom Park, or face civil disobedience from 28 November. Home Minister Priyank Kharge says the government is studying other protest sites and does not intend to curb protest rights.
  • Nyala: Drone strike on Nyala market kills dozens. A drone strike on a busy market in Nyala, South Darfur, on Monday evening killed at least 36 people and wounded over 150, MSF said, attributing it to Sudan's army; the rights group Emergency Lawyers says more than 100 died. The army has not commented. The RSF controls Nyala.
  • Hebron: UN rights chief warns of Hebron ethnic cleansing. More than 3,000 Palestinians have been forced from their homes in Israel's Hebron operation, begun after two soldiers were killed at a checkpoint on Friday, the UN says. Volker Türk called it collective punishment and warned of 'serious concerns of ethnic cleansing'. No Israeli response to his statement has been reported.
  • Gaza: Gaza aid paused as Israel shuts crossing. UN aid transport in Gaza was suspended on Tuesday after Israel closed the Kerem Shalom crossing for its election day, the UN says. About 950,000 people live in displacement sites at medium to high risk of flooding as a fourth winter in tents nears.
  • Moyale: 36,600 flee Ethiopian clashes into Kenya. About 36,600 people have fled fighting between Somali and Oromia regional forces in southern Ethiopia into northern Kenya, the UN migration agency says; nearly 11,000 shelter in a church compound and the rest with host families. Kenya's government leads the response; no statement from Ethiopia's federal government has been reported.

item.title: Resistance Daily · Tue 27 Oct 2026
item.description:
• Pasighat: 26 arrested over Pasighat violence; hunger strike. East Siang police said on Monday that 26 people, five of them juveniles, are arrested over the 23 October arson in Pasighat, with eight cases filed, and urged people not to share unverified information; anti-dam activists Ebo Mili and Otul Jerang reportedly began a hunger strike in custody. Six more are held for questioning.
  • Mumbai: Actor's challenge to 'Leave India' notice deferred. The Bombay High Court moved to Tuesday actor Imran Khan's challenge to a notice, citing the Immigration and Foreigners Act, to leave India by 28 October after police detained him near an election-roll protest; the US citizen and OCI cardholder says he got no hearing, and the Solicitor General appeared for the Union. Police detained him on 10 October.
  • Chhattisgarh: Supreme Court to hear challenge to conversion law. The Supreme Court on Monday issued notice to the Centre and Chhattisgarh on a tribal Christian group's challenge to the state's 2026 anti-conversion law, which requires a public declaration before changing faith; neither government's response has been reported. The court tagged it with challenges to similar laws in Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan.
  • El Fasher: A year after RSF takeover, thousands may be held. A year after the RSF captured El Fasher, Human Rights Watch says thousands of civilians may still be in RSF detention and the UN rights office estimates more than 6,000 were killed in three days; the RSF did not respond to Amnesty's findings. Amnesty says fewer than 70,000 people remain.
  • Gaza: Strike on Mawasi camp kills girl, 7. At least five people were killed in Gaza on Monday, four of them, including 7-year-old Jouri al-Soufi, in a strike on a displacement camp in al-Mawasi, Nasser Hospital said; Israel's military told AFP it was looking into the reports. Medical sources count 1,559 killed since the ceasefire.
  • Tirana: Albania plans curbs on protests after clashes. After weekend clashes in which police used tear gas, water cannon and rubber bullets, Prime Minister Edi Rama, blaming the opposition and 'foreign actors', announced a bill to let police limit protests near public institutions and fine protesters up to €5,000; activists warn it threatens assembly and speech. It would also criminalise online calls for violence.
  • Nairobi: Arrests at Nairobi fuel-price march. Police arrested several protesters in running battles in central Nairobi on Monday during a march against fuel prices, after petrol rose to Sh226.96 a litre; no police statement or arrest count was reported. Organisers, the Coalition of Human Rights Defenders, say they notified police on 22 October.

item.title: Resistance Daily · Mon 26 Oct 2026
item.description:
• Pasighat: Curbs stay in Pasighat as CM meets groups. Prohibitory orders stayed in force in parts of East Siang on Sunday; officials reported no fresh violence. Chief Minister Pema Khandu met community organisations and MLAs, blaming “misinformation” for fears over the Siang dam. Protest groups want the project scrapped, armed forces withdrawn and 10 arrested activists freed.
  • Delhi: Jamia students end protest after union deal. Police kept students out of Jamia's locked campus on Sunday and detained some; police say two women held outside were released and a man was put in preventive detention. Students later ended their two-week protest after the university agreed to hold union elections, absent since 2006, and withdraw suspensions.
  • Bengaluru: Officials filed 61,059 voter-deletion forms without reasons. Election officials themselves filed at least 61,059 forms to delete names from Karnataka's rolls, none stating the reason the rules require, The Hindu found; most came after the 23 September deadline. Officials say the system auto-generated them when voters could not be reached. The final roll is due 27 October.
  • Gaza: Eight killed, three at Gaza university. Israeli strikes killed at least eight people across Gaza on Sunday, including three security guards at the Islamic University in Gaza City; seven female students were hurt in an earlier strike on the campus. Gaza's Health Ministry counts 1,551 killed since the ceasefire. No Israeli military comment was reported.
  • Hebron: Over 2,670 displaced in Hebron, Palestinian officials say. More than 2,670 people, mostly women, children and elderly people, have been displaced by Israel's Hebron operation, the Palestinian prime minister's office said on Sunday, citing the municipality. Troops ordered residents of Ein Deir Baha to leave. Israel's public broadcaster reports the army will end the operation within days.
  • Taraba: Toll in Taraba village attack rises to 40. Amnesty International says at least 40 people were killed when armed men attacked Binnari village on Friday, burning homes, shops and food; police had earlier confirmed 10 deaths, and many people are missing. Police say officers were deployed to restore order; no group has been named.
  • DR Congo: Nurse killed responding to Ebola alert. A nurse was killed and another health worker badly injured on Saturday in Bafwasende, Tshopo province, while responding to an Ebola alert, the WHO says. Local authorities have not commented. The outbreak, Congo's deadliest, has recorded more than 9,800 cases and 4,700 deaths since May.
  • France: France reports 1,314 arrests; Italy arrests nine. France reported 1,314 arrests at Saturday's cost-of-living protests, with 53 officers hurt and two people seriously injured; the interior minister blamed “radical activists”. Italy arrested nine and took 371 people, 110 of them minors, for checks; its prime minister said peaceful protest must be protected.
  • Malaysia: Malaysia orders CID probe into custody death. Malaysia's police chief ordered the CID to investigate the death of Noorizwan Zulkefly, 42, who died on 1 October after 12 days in Cheras police custody, citing unusual injuries. Family lawyers say an autopsy found brain bleeding from head trauma; police still class it as sudden death.

item.title: Resistance Daily · Sun 25 Oct 2026
item.description:
• Siang: Pasighat under gathering ban after dam unrest. After Friday night's arson in Pasighat, police detained five youths for questioning and barred gatherings of more than five people from Saturday evening; activists including lawyer Ebo Mili surrendered, saying the bandh was peaceful. Chief Minister Pema Khandu offered talks, saying the government's doors are open.
  • Kashmir: Six, including four women, held under UAPA. Bandipora police announced on Saturday the arrest of six people, four of them women, under the anti-terror UAPA. Police allege a network linked to the banned Ittihad-ul-Muslimeen spread separatist ideology and received about ₹8 lakh; no response from the accused or their families was reported.
  • Vijayawada: CBI books seven police over custodial death. On the High Court's direction, the CBI has booked seven people, including a suspended inspector, over the death of 25-year-old Gade Sai Krishna. His mother alleges he was illegally detained and tortured at Krishnalanka police station and his body burned; the accused have not been tried.
  • Manipur: Imphal sit-in against any division of Manipur. Five civil society groups led by AMUCO held a sit-in in Imphal East on Saturday, starting a statewide agitation against any administrative division of Manipur; their six demands include repeal of AFSPA and rehabilitation of displaced people. No police action or government response was reported.
  • France: 410,000–800,000 march in France; ~1,000 arrested. Between 410,000 (interior ministry) and about 800,000 (organisers) marched on Saturday over schools and living costs. Police used tear gas in Paris, Lyon, Nantes and other cities, where some protests were banned. The interior minister reported nearly 1,000 arrests and "an extremely elevated level of violence."
  • Hebron: Families displaced in Hebron military operation. About 250 families, almost 1,200 people according to Hebron's municipality, were displaced as Israeli forces entered Hebron on Saturday after two soldiers were killed; demolitions began near the attack site. The military says it is dismantling "terrorist infrastructure" and removing structures that pose a security threat.
  • Gaza: Two killed in Gaza despite ceasefire. A woman was shot dead in Beit Lahia and a man killed by a drone strike in Gaza City on Saturday, medical sources said. Gaza's Health Ministry says 1,547 people have been killed since the ceasefire began. No Israeli military comment on these deaths was reported.
  • El Fasher: Drone strikes; ex-detainees describe torture. Drones residents attribute to the army hit El Fasher's market on Thursday, killing civilians and fighters, Darfur24 reports. Amnesty says fewer than 70,000 people remain a year after the RSF took the city and former detainees describe torture. Neither the army nor the RSF has responded.

item.title: Resistance Daily · Sat 24 Oct 2026
item.description:
• Pasighat: Tear gas and arson during Siang dam bandh. Police fired tear gas during Friday's 12-hour bandh against the Siang Upper dam project, and four to five women were hospitalised. Protesters later reportedly set fire to an NHPC office, a police station and police vehicles. Police say protesters threw stones and defied prohibitory orders. Protesters want 10 arrested activists freed.
  • Imphal: Tear gas at Imphal protest over killings. Thousands joined a 'sound protest' in five valley districts on Friday against continuing killings, four days after three people were killed in Kangpokpi district. Police fired tear gas near the governor's residence in Imphal; no injuries were reported. The state Home Minister says three people have been held.
  • Delhi: Marchers detained near Election Commission. Police stopped a march against the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls on Ashoka Road on Friday, short of the Election Commission's headquarters, and detained protesters. Outlook reports more than 100 detained; Scroll says several. Police had asked the marchers to leave the area; no official count was reported.
  • Delhi HC: Court upholds peace-bond notice to student leader. The Delhi High Court on Friday rejected student leader Neha Bora's plea against a magistrate's notice to sign a ₹10,000 bond to keep the peace. She was detained at a 16 October protest near Barakhamba Road. The court found 'adequate safeguards' and ordered that she be given all materials.
  • Bengaluru: Bengaluru march allowed after placards lowered. More than 200 people marched from Town Hall to Freedom Park on Friday against the electoral-roll revision; it began only after they lowered placards police objected to. The DCP said permission was conditional and covered a march with the Tricolour and constitutional placards, not a protest.
  • Sudan: UN: drones killed 306 in Sudan in October. The UN human rights office says drone strikes it attributes to both the army and the RSF killed at least 306 people in the first three weeks of October, hitting homes, markets, hospitals and displacement sites. The Security Council condemned the Abyei market attack. Neither force's response was reported.
  • Karak: Gunmen kill seven at church funeral in Jordan. Gunmen opened fire during a funeral at a church in Hmoud, Karak governorate, on Friday, killing at least seven people and wounding 34. No one has claimed the attack. Jordan's interior minister called it an 'unprecedented' terrorist attack, and the search for the gunmen continues.
  • Trappes: One killed in suspected racist shooting near Paris. A gunman killed one person and wounded four to five others, including a 12-year-old girl, in Trappes and La Verrière on Friday. A 39-year-old suspect is in custody. Anti-terror prosecutors are examining whether victims were targeted for race or religion; the Élysée called it a 'racist, terrorist attack'.
  • Hebron: West Bank lockdown after two soldiers killed. Israel ordered a full West Bank lockdown after an attack in Hebron killed two Israeli soldiers; the military says it killed two gunmen. Palestinian bodies report 36 arrests and 17 attacks on olive farmers on Thursday; no Israeli comment on these was reported. The UN says closures severely restrict movement and livelihoods.
  • Taiz: UN: 800,000 in Taiz cut off from aid. UN agencies say Taiz City has been cut off for 20 days by fighting between Houthi forces and government troops. WFP says more than 800,000 people are cut off from assistance; water production has halved and truck water costs have tripled. No response from either side was reported.
  • France: France bans rallies, deploys 70,000 police. France is deploying about 70,000 police on Saturday and several cities have banned or rerouted protests after last weekend's rioting; 217 people have been jailed since, the justice minister says. The interior minister cited online calls for violence. Unions call the bans an abuse of authority and are challenging them in court.

item.title: Resistance Daily · Fri 23 Oct 2026
item.description:
• Pasighat: Siang dam opponents begin 24-hour sit-in. Opponents of the 11,000 MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project began a 24-hour sit-in in Pasighat on Thursday, demanding the release of detained activists and an end to surveys; five more activists were reportedly taken into custody. The district allowed the sit-in but barred any march, and says law and order is a separate matter from dam opposition.
  • Manipur: Manipur valley sit-ins; students detained near Kangla. Sit-ins were held across Manipur's valley districts on Thursday over the killing of three firewood collectors at Khongban Sunurok; schools stayed shut. Security forces clashed with student marchers near Kangla Gate in Imphal and several people were detained. No police or government statement on Thursday's protests was reported.
  • Ladakh: Ladakh talks with the Centre called off. A 22 October round of talks between the Home Ministry and the Leh Apex Body and Kargil Democratic Alliance did not take place, Sonam Wangchuk said, accusing the Centre of going back on a May understanding. The groups seek a Union Territory with a legislature and safeguards. The ministry has not commented.
  • Delhi: Released protest leaders seek time from police. A day after leaving Tihar, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka did not appear for Crime Branch questioning on Thursday over two FIRs linked to the 13 October Jantar Mantar protest, and asked for more time. Police are expected to serve a fresh notice.
  • Abyei: Khartoum denies Abyei strike; probe sought. Sudan's foreign ministry said the army has 'absolutely no connection' to Monday's drone strike on Amiet Market, which Abyei officials say killed 153 people, buried in two mass graves; it gave no evidence. The RSF-aligned authorities, who blame the army, asked the UN fact-finding mission to investigate. The African Union condemned the strikes.
  • Blue Nile: Blue Nile detainees held without lawyers. The rights group HUDO says a joint security cell arrested at least eight civilians in Roseires between 12 and 17 October on suspicion of links to the SPLA-N rebels, including an aid official and a Red Crescent volunteer, and holds them in Damazin without access to lawyers or family. No official response is reported.
  • Gaza: Four killed in Gaza despite ceasefire. Israeli strikes and gunfire killed at least four people across Gaza on Thursday, in Gaza City, Khan Younis, near Nuseirat and near Jabalia, where a woman was shot, according to agency reports. Israel's military said it struck Hamas in three of the places and was not aware of the Jabalia incident.
  • West Bank: Settler suspects freed; olive harvest attacks continue. A Jerusalem court released nine of ten settlers held over assaults on a Washington Post photojournalist and European diplomats to house arrest; police say one remains in custody. On Thursday settlers burned olive trees near Imatin and stole olives near Yabad, Wafa reports. UN officials said attacks on olive farmers 'must stop'.
  • Tunisia: Tunisia clashes after two deaths linked to police. Police fired tear gas at protesters in the Tunis suburb of Ettadhamen after a man detained on suspicion of drug dealing died; his family blames police abuse, while local media report he swallowed drugs. In Jebiniana, relatives say a man died while chased by security forces. No official statement is reported.
  • Georgia: Georgian journalist arrested on treason charge. Georgia's Prosecutor's Office arrested Domenti Chubinidze of the newspaper Asaval-Dasavali on a treason (sabotage) charge over his reporting on the David Gareji monastery complex; it faces up to four years. Prosecutors say he acted against the state's interests and will seek pretrial detention.
  • Mali: HRW reports drone deaths and torture in Mali. Human Rights Watch says an apparent army drone strike killed eight civilians in Guélédié on 16 September, and that detainees at a Sévaré base were held in a metal container and beaten, given electric shocks and waterboarded. The army said it 'neutralized' terrorists there; Mali and Russia did not reply to HRW.

item.title: Resistance Daily · Thu 22 Oct 2026
item.description:
• Delhi: Jantar Mantar pair freed; UN experts seek probe. A Delhi magistrate on Wednesday ordered the release of Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, jailed over a Jantar Mantar protest, rejecting a police request for three more days' custody. On Tuesday two dozen UN experts urged an independent inquiry into force used at the protests; India has said police acted strictly in accordance with the law.
  • Delhi: Century-old Delhi mosque told to vacate. The Land and Development Office told the Race Course mosque near the Prime Minister's residence to vacate within six days, calling it unauthorised on government land; the Delhi Waqf Board says it is Waqf property notified in 1977. Nearly 700 nearby families were displaced; police say they were given homes in Mundka.
  • Manipur: Tear gas in Imphal; Kuki man shot dead. Police fired tear gas on Wednesday as protesters over Monday's killing of three Meitei firewood collectors tried to enter an Imphal event attended by the Chief Minister; three people had minor injuries. A Kuki man, Paolen Khongsai, was shot dead on Tuesday. Police have arrested three suspects in Monday's ambush.
  • Srinagar: Court summons Srinagar magistrate over PSA order. The Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh High Court ordered Srinagar's District Magistrate to appear in person with the full record and explain why he allegedly passed a Public Safety Act detention order against Zubair Amin Bangroo 'recklessly and mechanically'. The order alleges links to militants; the authorities' reply is not reported.
  • Abyei: Abyei market strike toll rises to 153. Abyei's caretaker information minister says Monday's drone strike on Amiet Market killed at least 153 people, up from 73, with fires still burning; MSF is treating more than 20 wounded. South Sudan blames Sudan's army. A senior Sudanese officer told AP the army hit RSF-bound fuel tankers and does not target civilians.
  • Portugal: Police clear Portugal housing-protest camps. Police cleared cost-of-living protest camps in Lisbon's Rossio Square before dawn and arrested 55 people, released pending a court appearance; protesters returned within hours, and organisers count over 1,000 at each camp in Lisbon and Porto. Police called the eviction 'calm, proportionate'; a camp spokesperson called it 'very aggressive'.
  • Burkina Faso: Burkina Faso restores the death penalty. Burkina Faso's unelected transitional parliament unanimously adopted a penal code restoring the death penalty for high treason, terrorism, espionage and other crimes, Human Rights Watch reports; it had been abolished for ordinary crimes in 2018. The justice minister called it a necessary measure to combat terrorism.
  • N. Korea: UN experts: fate of returned North Koreans unknown. UN-appointed experts said the fate of many people forcibly returned to North Korea from China since 2023 is unknown, citing risks of disappearance, torture and forced labour, and urged China to stop the returns. The UN report carries no response from China or North Korea.
